text:
3:12, every Thursday. Mara found the book in the bread rack. Same one every time: The Practical Guide to Inland Birds, cracked blue spine, library stamp from a town forty miles away. She'd set it on the flour bin, wipe butter off the cover. She'd mean to take it back after her shift. By noon, errands and the heat and sleep would swallow that thought. Next Thursday it'd be there again, tucked in between the cooling rye loaves.
Tonight the bakery hummed. Proofing cabinet, old radio static, rain pressing silver lines down the front window. Mara lifted the book with both hands, kind of like it might be warm. A folded receipt marked the chapter on herons. She opened it.
In block letters, someone had written: I THINK YOU ARE THE ONLY PERSON AWAKE WHEN I AM. PAGE 47.
She turned to page 47. Grey heron in a marsh, one foot raised, patient as a saint. Under the picture in pencil: THURSDAY, 3:30?
The clock over the mixer clicked once.
Mara brushed flour off her apron, unlocked the front door, turned on the little OPEN sign.
